en.name: Ponzu
en.summary: Ponzu is soy sauce cut with citrus juice and dashi — thinner, brighter and more delicate than plain soy sauce, and shorter-lived for the same reason. Unopened it keeps about 12–24 months in the cupboard. Once opened, refrigerate it and use within about 1 month.
en.pantry: Unopened bottles keep to the printed date in a cool dark cupboard, about 12–24 months from purchase — that range is what commercial bottles print rather than an agency figure. Keep them upright, away from the hob and out of the sun. After opening, the cupboard is the wrong place: the citrus aroma that is the whole point of ponzu is the first casualty of a bottle left on the counter, and the dilution means it has less salt working for it than a straight soy sauce does.
en.fridge: Refrigerate once opened, at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and use within about 1 month — a figure borrowed from opened soy sauce, which if anything is generous here, since ponzu is that sauce diluted with citrus and dashi. Cap it tightly between uses and do not leave it out through a long meal at the table. Homemade ponzu, made with fresh-squeezed juice and no pasteurisation, should be treated as a fresh food: keep it cold and use it within a week or two.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for ponzu and freezing it is self-defeating: the fresh citrus top notes are exactly what freezing and thawing drive off, and they are the reason to buy ponzu in the first place. Buy a small bottle instead, or make it fresh in the quantity you need — a homemade ponzu takes minutes and tastes better than any bottle a month after opening.
spoilage: Cloudiness or a film on the surface of a previously clear sauce
A sour, fermented or off smell rather than a bright citrus-and-soy one
Sediment that was not there before, together with a flat taste
Mould around the neck or cap
tips: Buy small bottles; the opened window is measured in weeks, not months.
Write the opening date on the bottle.
Never pour leftover dipping sauce from the table back into the bottle.
Make your own with fresh citrus, soy and a little dashi when you want it at its best.

faq.q: How long does ponzu last once opened?
faq.a: About 1 month refrigerated at 4 °C or below. That figure comes from opened soy sauce; ponzu is more dilute, so do not stretch it.

faq.q: Does ponzu need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Yes, once opened. It is soy sauce diluted with citrus and dashi, so it has less salt protecting it than plain soy sauce.

faq.q: How long does an unopened bottle of ponzu keep?
faq.a: About 12–24 months in a cool dark cupboard, to the printed date.

faq.q: How long does homemade ponzu keep?
faq.a: Treat it as a fresh food: refrigerated, and used within a week or two.

zh.name: 柚子醋醬油
zh.summary: Ponzu 是醬油加柑橘汁和日式高湯調成的——比純醬油更稀、更清亮、也更細緻，而且正因如此更不耐放。未開封放櫥櫃大約 12～24 個月。開封後請冷藏，並在大約 1 個月內用完。
zh.pantry: 未開封的瓶子放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃，到標示日期為止，從購買日起算大約 12～24 個月——這個範圍是市售瓶身標示的，不是主管機關的數字。請直立擺放、遠離爐火、避免日曬。開封之後，櫥櫃就是錯的地方：柚子醋最重要的那股柑橘香，正是一瓶擱在檯面上時最先陣亡的東西，而且稀釋也意味著它的鹽度比純醬油低。
zh.fridge: 開封後請放 4 °C 以下冷藏，並在大約 1 個月內用完——這個數字借自開封後的醬油，對柚子醋來說甚至算寬鬆，因為它就是被柑橘和高湯稀釋過的醬油。每次用完蓋緊，也不要在一頓長時間的聚餐中一直擱在桌上。自製柚子醋用的是現榨果汁、沒有殺菌，請當成新鮮食品：保持低溫，並在一兩週內用完。
zh.freezer: 柚子醋沒有冷凍期限，而冷凍本身就自相矛盾：新鮮柑橘的前味正是一凍一解最先散掉的東西，而那又是買柚子醋的理由。與其冷凍，不如買小瓶，或要用時現做——自製柚子醋只要幾分鐘，味道也勝過一瓶開封一個月的市售品。
spoilage: 原本清澈的醬汁變混濁，或表面浮膜
聞起來發酸、有發酵味或異味，而不是明亮的柑橘與醬油香
出現原本沒有的沉澱，味道也變得扁平
tips: 買小瓶；開封後的窗口是以「週」而不是「月」計。
桌上用剩的沾醬絕對不要倒回瓶子。
想要最好的風味，就用新鮮柑橘、醬油加一點高湯自己調。

faq.q: 柚子醋開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 放 4 °C 以下冷藏大約 1 個月。這個數字來自開封後的醬油，而柚子醋更稀，所以不要再往上放寬。
開封後要。它是被柑橘和高湯稀釋過的醬油，保護它的鹽度比純醬油低。

faq.q: 未開封的柚子醋可以放多久？
faq.a: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃大約 12～24 個月，以標示日期為準。

faq.q: 自製柚子醋可以放多久？
faq.a: 請當成新鮮食品：冷藏，並在一兩週內用完。
